questions.text: Consider a complete binary tree where the left and the right subtrees of the root are max-heaps. The lower bound for the number of operations to convert the tree to a heap is
questions.solution:
Both subtrees are already heaps, so only the root may be out of place. One heapify (sift-down) from the root fixes it, moving down at most the height of the tree.

Bound = [latex]\Omega(\log n)[/latex] (and this is enough).

Answer: [latex]\Omega(\log n)[/latex]

questions.text: A binary tree T has 20 leaves. The number of nodes in T having two children is _______.
questions.solution:
In any binary tree, (nodes with 2 children) = (leaves) [latex]-[/latex] 1.

20 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 19

Answer: 19

questions.text: A software requirements specification (SRS) document should avoid discussing which one of the following?
questions.solution:
An SRS says what the system must do (functional and non-functional needs, interfaces, UI requirements). How it is built (the design) belongs in the design document.

Answer: Design specification
